title: Temperature-matched TESS counts do not separate a radiative-core CPV effect from the hot-star boundary
abstract: We test whether the lack of complex periodic variables (CPVs) in stars assigned a radiative core gives evidence beyond a temperature boundary. We reproduce 77 CPVs in 855 young rapid rotators and none in 125 core stars. Core status and a published 3450 K cut agree for 92.9% of stars. All 61 stars where they disagree have no CPVs. In 100 K temperature bins and bins of width 0.25 in ln(corotation radius / stellar radius), only 10 core stars share strata with detected CPVs. Equal observed odds predict 0.837 core detections there. The exact probability of zero is 0.398, and the one-sided 95% upper odds-ratio bound is 4.08. Adding age class gives no informative strata at 50 or 100 K resolution for either tested radius method. Twenty-three of 24 temperature-plus-radius bin tests without age strata permit equal odds. Bounded rate fits show that core and temperature terms both improve on the radius-only model. A temperature cut selected inside training folds gives poor predictions for the youngest class. The hot-star deficit is real in these labels, but the present sample does not robustly assign it to a core effect separate from temperature. Selected targets, model-derived core status, finite bins and uncertain efficiencies limit inference. We provide all aggregate tests, original analysis code, attributed parameter code, exact input hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps.
